QuestionStmt.S: What is the approximate mass of the precipitate formed when 50 mL of 16.9% solution of AgNO₃ is mixed with 50 mL of 7.45% KCl solution? (Molar mass of AgNO₃ = 169 g/mol, KCl = 74.5 g/mol, AgCl = 143.3 g/mol)

Solution.S:
Step 1: Calculate the mass of AgNO₃ in 50 mL of 16.9% solution.

16.9% means 16.9 g AgNO₃ in 100 mL solution.
So, in 50 mL: mass = (16.9/100) × 50 = 8.45 g.

Step 2: Calculate moles of AgNO₃.
Moles = mass / molar mass = 8.45 / 169 = 0.05 mol.

Step 3: Calculate the mass of KCl in 50 mL of 7.45% solution.
7.45% means 7.45 g KCl in 100 mL solution.
In 50 mL: mass = (7.45/100) × 50 = 3.725 g.

Step 4: Calculate moles of KCl.
Moles = 3.725 / 74.5 = 0.05 mol.

Step 5: The reaction is AgNO₃ + KCl → AgCl↓ + KNO₃.
Both react in 1:1 ratio, and moles are equal (0.05 mol each), so no limiting reagent; complete precipitation occurs.

Step 6: Moles of AgCl formed = 0.05 mol.
Mass of AgCl = moles × molar mass = 0.05 × 143.3 = 7.165 g ≈ 7 g.

Final Answer: $$\boxed{7 \text{ g}}$$

Hence, the correct option is B.
